Before anything is deleted, the shop saves one last backup by itself and downloads it. If that backup fails, the reset stops and nothing is deleted. Passo 6. TODO[PT] Read the warning. Then type the word RESET (in capital letters) in the box. Agora você deve ver: TODO[PT] the reset button lights up. It stays off until the word is typed exactly right — this is on purpose, so nobody can tap it by accident. Passo 7. TODO[PT] Tap the reset button, and confirm. ■ Screenshot — TODO[PT] Typing RESET to arm the reset button Capture d’écran — TODO[PT] Typing RESET to arm the reset button (task9-typereset.png — added when the final app is ready / ajoutée quand l’appli finale est prête) Agora você deve ver: TODO[PT] you are signed out. The shop is empty and new. Sign in again with admin / admin123 and pick a new password (same as Task 1).

entries.title: TODO[PT] [If something goes wrong] The reset button stays off: the word must be
entries.text: TODO[PT] [If something goes wrong] The reset button stays off: the word must be exactly RESET, all capitals, no spaces. Check Caps Lock. TODO[PT] [If something goes wrong] “PRE-RESET BACKUP FAILED”: the safety backup could not be saved, so the reset did not happen and nothing was deleted. Do Task 8 by hand, then try again. TODO[PT] Task 10 — When a sale fails because the internet dropped TODO[PT] Your shop lives on the internet. Every sale is recorded on the internet the moment it happens. If the internet drops in the middle of a sale, the sale cannot finish. Here is exactly what happens, and what to do. Good news first: nobody is charged, and your cart (what the customer is buying) stays on the screen. Nothing is lost. Passo 1. TODO[PT] Read the message on the screen. It will say the shop could not be reached, and the sale did not go through. ■ Screenshot — TODO[PT] The “could not reach the shop” message at checkout Capture d’écran — TODO[PT] The “could not reach the shop” message at checkout (task10-saleerror.png — added when the final app is ready / ajoutée quand l’appli finale est prête) Agora você deve ver: TODO[PT] your cart is still there, with every item, exactly as it was. Passo 2. TODO[PT] Check the Wi-Fi: look for the fan-shaped icon on the device. If it is missing or has an “!”, the device lost the internet. Passo 3. TODO[PT] Wait for the internet to come back (the icon returns). This can take a minute after an outage. Passo 4. TODO[PT] Tap Retry (or complete the sale again, the same way as Task 4). Agora você deve ver: TODO[PT] the receipt, like a normal sale. The sale is recorded once — retrying does not charge twice. TODO[PT] [If something goes wrong] If the customer cannot wait: there is no “offline” selling — a sale that never reached the internet simply never happened. Write down what they bought on paper if you like, and ring it in when the internet returns. TODO[PT] [If something goes wrong] If sales keep failing for a long time, the problem is the internet connection or the shop’s server — not the till. Tell the person who installed the shop. TODO[PT] More parts of the shop (in plain words) TODO[PT] The Catalogue TODO[PT] The Catalogue is your stock list: what you have, how many, and where it sits on the shelf. It is a different list from the Point of Sale products (Task 3). Something in the Catalogue marked “in store” can be scanned straight into a sale. You can also add many items at once from a spreadsheet file (this is called a CSV file), and look items up by their barcode/ISBN number. Donations, fair days

entries.title: and special orders (a customer asking you to order something in) each have their
entries.text: and special orders (a customer asking you to order something in) each have their own simple flow. TODO[PT] Appointments TODO[PT] Appointments is a booking book: customers book a time, and two bookings cannot take the same time by accident. TODO[PT] Classifieds — your shop’s buy-and-sell board TODO[PT] Classifieds is your shop’s own classified-ads board, like a small Kijiji built into your store. Create ads with photos, a price and a description; mark them For sale, Free, Services, Wanted, Jobs, Events or Announcements. Published ads appear on your public storefront, where buyers can save them as favourites. TODO[PT] My listings — free ads for everyone TODO[PT] Anyone can post free local ads — no shop needed. Open My listings and post with photos and a price. Free accounts can keep up to 15 ads active and post up to 5 new ads a day; ads stay up for 60 days and can be renewed. TODO[PT] Locked out? Get back in without email TODO[PT] You never need email to recover your account. At sign-up you receive recovery codes — one-time codes to keep somewhere safe. On the sign-in screen, choose “Forgot password?” then “Use a recovery code” to set a new password. You can also set security questions in Settings — Account. TODO[PT] Files TODO[PT] Files keeps your documents and pictures in the shop, and you can search the words inside them. TODO[PT] Certificates — the staff time clock TODO[PT] Staff clock in and out with their own secret number (a PIN — a short number, like a bank card’s). Managers can fix a punch, make the schedule (two shifts for the same person cannot overlap), and print attestations — signed papers that prove someone’s hours. Volunteer/community hours are kept separate from paid hours. Team members are invited with a code and have a role: Owner (can do everything), Manager (almost everything), Cashier (sells). TODO[PT] Taxes — read this before your first real sale TODO[PT] A new shop charges no tax at all until you set it up. That is on purpose, so nobody is charged the wrong tax. Before selling for real, ask your accountant (the person who does your taxes) two things: what tax percentages apply where you are, and whether each tax is calculated on the price alone, or on price-plus-the-other-tax. Then, in the Point of Sale settings, type those numbers in, and press Save. The shop never changes tax numbers by itself. Some organizations pay no tax: they can be marked tax-exempt so their receipts show no tax. TODO[PT] Other settings

entries.title: • TODO[PT] Colours and light/dark: Settings · Appearance.
entries.text: • TODO[PT] Colours and light/dark: Settings · Appearance. • TODO[PT] If someone else changes a setting on another till, your screen picks it up within about a minute. If you are in the middle of typing in a form, your typing is never erased by that. • TODO[PT] When a newer version of the shop is ready, a small message invites you to refresh the page. Nothing is forced on you mid-sale. TODO[PT] When something goes wrong TODO[PT] This shop is built to fail politely: it explains, it never shows a blank page, and it never silently loses a sale. Here are the bad moments we know about, in plain words. TODO[PT] The shop cannot be reached at opening • TODO[PT] Before opening, the shop checks itself. If its own connection settings look wrong (for example a cut-off key), the screen says the setup looks wrong and that no password will work until whoever installed the shop fixes it. If the settings are fine but the server does not answer, the screen says that instead. Either way there is a Retry button — tap it once the internet is back. TODO[PT] One part of the shop stops working • TODO[PT] Each part of the shop is walled off from the others. If one part breaks, only that part shows a message, with a Retry button and a short code (like RS-9K2Q1-4F2A). Write the code down and tell whoever looks after the shop — it points straight at the problem. The rest of the shop keeps working. If the shop breaks three times in a row while opening, it starts in a safe mode with repair options instead of breaking again and again. TODO[PT] Dangerous buttons protect you • TODO[PT] Before anything destructive (deleting, voiding a gift card, removing a time punch), the shop quietly saves a small safety copy on the device — the last 3 are kept. That is a safety net, not a backup: still do Task 8 regularly. TODO[PT] Getting help • TODO[PT] Open Help & Guide from the Start menu (the Start menu is the main menu button of the shop) — this guide lives there too. From the sign-in screen, you can also send a support message. TODO[PT] Honest limits — what this shop cannot do TODO[PT] We would rather tell you the limits than let you discover them. Here they are, plainly. • TODO[PT] No internet, no selling. There is no offline mode on purpose: a sale is only real once it is recorded on the internet. (Task 10 shows what happens.) • TODO[PT] The public page is a shop window, not a website. Its look is fixed, and customers cannot buy or pay on it. For a full custom website, you need a website tool as well.

entries.title: • TODO[PT] Loyalty points are “best effort”. If the power or internet dies at th
entries.text: • TODO[PT] Loyalty points are “best effort”. If the power or internet dies at the exact split second between recording a sale and adding points, the sale is safe but the points might not be added. • TODO[PT] Brand-new gift card glitch (rare). If a gift card is sold and the internet drops at that exact moment, the recorded sale can end up pointing at a card that was cancelled during cleanup. If a customer says a brand-new card does not work, look in History first — a manager can void that sale. • TODO[PT] Your sign-in lives in the browser. Whoever can open your unlocked browser on your device is, in practice, signed in as you. Sign out on shared devices. There is no list of “which devices are signed in”: signing out works on that device, and if the master account resets your password, you are signed out everywhere at once. • TODO[PT] Safety copies live on the same device. If the device is lost or wiped, they are gone. Your downloaded backup file (Task 8) is the copy that lives elsewhere — keep it. • TODO[PT] Taxes start at zero. Until you set them (see “Taxes” above), no tax is charged at all. Ask your accountant before real selling. TODO[PT] Appendix — Installing on your own backend (technical) TODO[PT] This appendix is for the person installing the shop the very first time. It is the only technical part of this guide. If someone installed the shop for you, you can skip it. Passo 1. TODO[PT] Create a free project at supabase.com (Dashboard — New project). This is the shop’s “cloud”: where everything is saved. Passo 2. TODO[PT] Open the SQL editor and run every file in supabase/migrations/ in order, from 001 to the latest. One of them (056) creates the built-in master account (admin / admin123, see Task 1); another (057) adds the factory reset; 063 adds the public storefront page tables. Passo 3. TODO[PT] Copy the project URL and the anon key (Project Settings — API) into a .env file as VITE_SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY (see .env.example). Passo 4. TODO[PT] Run: npm install, then npm run build. Put the dist/ folder on any static host. Passo 5. TODO[PT] Open the shop and do Task 1 immediately — change the master password before anything else. • TODO[PT] Rebranding note: the master account’s email must match BRAND.accountsDomain in src/lib/brand.js. If you change the domain, update the email in migration 056 before running it (plain usernames are turned into <username>@<domain> at sign-in). TODO[PT] Closing line TODO[PT] Vendra — step-by-step guide. The words on the screen always win over this guide.
